properties.decision:
PARKED ON ANTHONY'S EXPLICIT WORD, 2026-08-25: *"park the rust-rocksdb migration with its reason."* **PARKED IS NOT REJECTED.** `dec:absorb-rocksdb-024-unchanged-then-switch-separately` stays `accepted`, its reasoning stays correct, and the switch stays owed if RocksDB stays.

THE REASON, IN ONE LINE: **it is an 86-file migration whose entire subject is the component that may be about to be retired.**

WHAT CHANGED SINCE THAT DECISION WAS MADE, ONE DAY EARLIER. On 2026-08-24 the switch was straightforwardly next: absorb `rocksdb` 0.24 verbatim, then swap the crate in its own PR with one variable and one revert. Nothing in that reasoning was wrong. What arrived a day later is a question that sits UNDER it — `dec:idea-does-reflow2-need-a-byte-store-at-all-or-only-durability`, asking whether an embedded key-value store earns its place at all. Three of that question's five blockers have since been measured away:

    load to fully searchable, no database at all      1,156 ms
    save (build export doc + serialize)                 265 ms
    confirmation-ledger claims surviving hydration    208 / 208, ZERO differing fields
    core tests passing with no store and no index         1,452

⇒ IF THAT QUESTION RESOLVES TOWARD THE DOCUMENT AS THE ENDURING ARTIFACT, `cmp:rocksdb-backend` is what gets retired — and the migration becomes work done and then deleted. Doing it first de-risks nothing; it spends the effort on the branch most likely to be cut.

⭐ THE ORDERING IS THE POINT, AND IT IS THE SAME PRINCIPLE THE PARKED DECISION ITSELF ARGUES. That decision exists because mixing a dependency swap into a migration gives a failure two candidate causes. The same discipline one level up says: do not migrate a component while its existence is an open question. **One variable at a time applies to WHETHER a thing exists, not only to how it is changed.**

🛑 THE FAILURE MODE THIS GUARDS AGAINST IS SPECIFIC AND LIKELY. The migration reads as tidy housekeeping — an unmaintained crate, a maintained replacement, and a version number that looks far behind (it is not: `rocksdb` 0.24 and `rust-rocksdb` 0.52 are different crates on independent numbering, and reading them as one series overstates the gap). AGENTS.md already warns against bumping the pin as housekeeping, but that warning explains the ~19-minute COMPILE cost, not this one. A session that reads the accepted decision and nothing else will correctly conclude the switch is owed and start it. **This node exists so that session meets the park.**

⚠️ WHAT UNPARKS IT: `dec:idea-does-reflow2-need-a-byte-store-at-all-or-only-durability` settling, either way.
- **RocksDB stays** → the switch is owed exactly as written, and this decision should be `superseded`.
- **RocksDB goes** → the switch is retired along with `cmp:rocksdb-backend`, and the parked decision is superseded rather than completed.

📌 A DIFFERENT PARK, NOT TO BE CONFUSED WITH THIS ONE: `dec:idea-a-byte-backend-that-compiles-in-seconds` (redb, fjall, LMDB, SQLite) is parked on Anthony's word of 2026-08-24 — *"still parked for a time"*. That one asks WHICH embedded engine. This one asks whether to move between two wrappers of the SAME engine. The question blocking both asks whether an embedded engine is needed at all.

📌 MODELLING NOTE, recorded because the vocabulary corrected the first attempt: this was first written as a TemporalFact and REFUSED — `basis` accepts only `measured` or `forecast`, and a park is neither. It is a choice somebody made, so it is a Decision. The schema pointed at the right node type rather than accepting a wrong one.

KEPT DISTINCT, after reading both: `dec:absorb-rocksdb-024-unchanged-then-switch-separately` is the decision to make the switch and it is unchanged by this — parking is a separate act, by a separate person, at a separate time, and folding it in would erase that. `cmp:rocksdb-backend` is the thing the switch would alter, not a statement about when to alter it.
properties.name: PARKED — do not start the rust-rocksdb migration until the store question settles; it is an 86-file change to the one component that may be retired
properties.rationale:
Recorded as its own Decision rather than by editing the parked one, deliberately: editing that node's text would mean re-sending the whole `decision` field and destroying its pre-image, which is the hazard `fact:the-revising-write-warning-fired-correctly-and-the-overwrite-happened-anyway` measured twice today.

Kept ACCEPTED rather than proposed because Anthony gave it in his own words as an instruction, not as a musing — asserting it would be forgery only if he had not said it.
